title: Minimum Degree of a Connected Trio in a Graph
summary: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and a list of edges, find the minimum degree of any connected trio.
statement: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and a list of edges, find the minimum degree of any connected trio. A connected trio consists of three nodes with edges between each pair. The degree of a trio is the count of edges connecting a node within the trio to a node outside it. Return -1 if no such trio exists.
constraints: The undirected simple graph uses one-indexed nodes.
For every fully connected three-node trio, its degree is the number of edges from trio nodes to outside nodes; return the minimum or -1.
target_time_complexity: O(sum over edges of intersection cost)
hints: A trio exists when two adjacent nodes share a third neighbor.
Store neighbor sets, intersect them for each ordered edge, and evaluate each trio once.
Its external degree is deg(a)+deg(b)+deg(c)-6 because three internal edges contribute two endpoints each.
Set intersection proves all three edges exist, and the ordering guards cover each unordered trio exactly once.
editorial: Set intersection proves all three edges exist, and the ordering guards cover each unordered trio exactly once.

tests.explanation: Trio 1,2,3 has three external incident edges, so its degree is three.
The only connected trio 5,6,7 has two outside edges.
